title: Marquesas Islands
summary: A volcanic archipelago in French Polynesia, northeast of Tahiti. Settled by seafarers around 1000 CE according to UNESCO, though Britannica cites inhabitation as early as 340 bce. Sighted by Europeans from 1595, annexed by France in 1842, and a UNESCO World Heritage site since 2024 for cultural and natural value.

as_recorded.value: a seafaring civilization that arrived around 1000 CE

where.modern_name: Marquesas Islands (Îles Marquises; Te Henua Enata), French Polynesia

importance.justification: Remote Polynesian archipelago with a distinct chiefdom culture and World Heritage status, but regional in historical reach.

reviewer_note: Sources disagree on settlement: Britannica says as early as 340 bce (with scholarly disagreement), UNESCO says around 1000 CE. I used 1000 CE as the start and 1842 annexation as the end, which is an editorial framing. UNESCO also mentions demographic collapse after European contact without giving figures.
